Who owns the position?
01
Make composition obligatory
STATED
PLAYED

Required policy sections enter each mechanism.

ALTERNATIVE NAMED IN PR

Keep optional numbers and local fallback defaults.

A missing policy input becomes a missing constructor argument; clocks, storage, paths and worker injection remain separate dependencies.

CLI constructors change; the policy package and its snapshot already exist. Mechanisms stay in apps/cli in this PR.

Reason on record: The PR says omitted composition must not recreate local defaults.

Analyze 01 ↗
Who owns the position?
02
Use the resource snapshot verbatim
STATED
PLAYED

Supervisor, ready record and worker heap use policy.resources.

BASE BEHAVIOR

Re-derive resources from effective memory or a separate memory cap.

The hard cap reported at readiness and the worker heap limit now come from the same supplied values. The CLI resource-policy class is deleted.

RSS hard / soft / resume limits; raw effective memory; V8 heap limit; 250 ms supervision; two replacements in ten minutes, then drain.

Reason on record: The policy record requires one complete snapshot across process and worker boundaries; the architecture spec gives thresholds one owner.

Analyze 02 ↗
Who owns the position?
03
Carry the output limits all the way through
STATED
PLAYED

Capture, spool, disk decode and both worker endpoints share output limits.

BASE BEHAVIOR

Give each output stage its own constants and optional capacities.

A record accepted by one stage is checked against the same chunk limit at later stages. Local CLI execution also consumes the output section.

64 KiB raw chunks → 256 KiB inline → 256 MiB per result → 512 MiB aggregate spool. These are existing defaults, not new tuning.

Reason on record: The PR explicitly routes output capture, spooling and worker validation through required output slices; the record states why each bound exists.

Analyze 03 ↗
Who owns the position?
04
Keep three framing capacities distinct
STATED
PLAYED

Ordinary JSON, execution control and raw binary chunks keep separate bounds.

COACH’S VARIATION · HYPOTHETICAL

Use one frame-size limit for all traffic.

The transfer decoder allows a binary envelope of control capacity plus chunk capacity; the codec separately checks raw chunk length. Socket write fragmentation remains an option.

8 MiB JSON; 256 KiB execution control; 64 KiB raw chunk. Numeric codec arguments replace imports of spool-owned constants.

Reason on record: The policy record distinguishes decoded control input, binary-transfer control and one raw record.

Analyze 04 ↗
Which clock is running?
05
Choose the timeout by caller purpose
STATED
PLAYED

Status observer: 100 ms. Ordinary transport: 250 ms.

ALTERNATIVE NAMED IN PR

Choose a timeout from the request’s kind.

The same identify or ping message can serve different callers. An execution-status request still uses the ordinary timeout; the word “status” does not select 100 ms.

The CLI status action sets responseTimeoutPurpose: status-observer. Ordinary is the default purpose. The constructor selects the value once.

Reason on record: The PR says status observation and ordinary execution-status requests have distinct deadlines.

Analyze 05 ↗
Which clock is running?
06
End the execution timer at acceptance
STATED
PLAYED

Policy supplies the 5 s admission timer; acceptance disables it.

COACH’S VARIATION · HYPOTHETICAL

Carry that timer into command completion.

Long accepted work keeps running without a completion deadline. Fetch and worker-output acknowledgement also retain their existing absence of a timer.

This is preserved behavior while the timer’s source changes. Healthy startup and unacknowledged-result retention likewise have no new expiry.

Reason on record: The policy record bounds admission without timing accepted completion; accepted work must not be replayed or failed for running long.

Analyze 06 ↗
How many chances remain?
07
Give recovery two independent budgets
STATED
PLAYED

Count execute reattachments outside; count fetch resumes inside each execute attempt.

ALTERNATIVE NAMED IN PR

Share a single used-retry flag across both recovery scopes.

A reattached execute attempt receives a fresh fetch allowance. Reattachment resends the same request identity after an authenticated accepted close; this is recovery, not local replay.

Default: one reattachment and one fetch resume per attempt. Base already nested the two scopes; this PR replaces fixed one-shot control with policy numbers. Added trace: execute → reattach → fetch.

Reason on record: The PR says every reattached execute attempt has its own fetch-resume allowance.

Analyze 07 ↗
How many chances remain?
08
Let the latest completion error escape
UNEXPLAINED
PLAYED

A later accepted completion failure is caught in the next loop iteration.

BASE BEHAVIOR

Always preserve the original accepted-close error.

When reattachment is accepted and its completion fails, the exposed error can now be that later failure. A failure before reattachment acceptance still rethrows the preceding error.

An effect of the numeric loop rewrite, separate from the stated reason for independent counters. No correctness verdict is attached.

Reason not found: No reason for this error-selection change was found in the PR, six commit messages, policy record or architecture spec.

Analyze 08 ↗
How many chances remain?
09
Keep the fetch path as one connection
UNEXPLAINED
PLAYED

Read a numeric resume allowance at the original execute socket; fetch itself has no retry loop.

COACH’S VARIATION · HYPOTHETICAL

Retry failed fetch connections until that numeric allowance is spent.

The code distinguishes an allowance from a complete repeated-fetch mechanism. Fetch failure rejects this attempt. The new reattachment test makes one fetch; it does not demonstrate repeated fetch failures with a limit above one.

Default limit is one. The limit check lives in executeOnce.resume(); fetchCompletion().catch(fail) exits the attempt. Outer recovery still has its own eligibility checks.

Reason not found: The PR explains independent counters, but does not explain retaining one fetch connection while accepting a numeric resume limit.

Analyze 09 ↗
Which clock is running?
10
Separate election grace from healthy warm-up
STATED
PLAYED

Use 15 s coordination grace for ownership; leave healthy readiness waiting unbounded.

COACH’S VARIATION · HYPOTHETICAL

Use “startup timeout” as one wall-clock deadline for every startup phase.

Registry ownership, daemon authorization and missing-owner observation consume the grace. A progressing warm-up does not expire because a large project takes time.

The unused startupTimeoutMs field is removed; the active grace is named coordinationGraceMs. Grace still has a scalar override on a registry helper (move 21).

Reason on record: The policy record preserves election recovery grace and explicitly gives progressing warm-up no project-size deadline.

Analyze 10 ↗
How many chances remain?
11
Count failed child launches explicitly
STATED
PLAYED

A local failure counter permits the configured number of fresh startup tries.

BASE BEHAVIOR

Use a hard-coded catch-and-try-once branch.

Only child exit or lost warm-up consumes this recovery route. Waiting for another owner does not reset the budget. Default one retry is preserved; tests exercise zero and two.

Retry limit counts retries after the first try: zero → one launch, two → up to three launches in the added tests.

Reason on record: The policy record preserves one fresh launch after a failed child; the PR routes retry behavior through numeric policy.

Analyze 11 ↗
Which clock is running?
12
Keep each cadence attached to its job
STATED
PLAYED

Wire separate policy leaves into heartbeat, authorization, observation and worker sampling.

COACH’S VARIATION · HYPOTHETICAL

Use one generic polling interval.

Equal or nearby intervals remain independently named. Worker sampling receives a projected number; process entries continue to receive the complete serialized snapshot.

100 ms heartbeat; 10 ms authorization; 20 ms readiness observation; 25 ms worker heap sampling; 250 ms RSS supervision (move 02).

Reason on record: The record preserves distinct authorization and observation cadences, live startup ownership and short-lived heap-peak observation.

Analyze 12 ↗
Which clock is running?
13
Preserve the shutdown time budget’s parts
STATED
PLAYED

Stop, escalation reserve, signal waits and acknowledgement polling use distinct leaves.

COACH’S VARIATION · HYPOTHETICAL

Collapse shutdown waits into one shared timeout.

A stop still reserves min(500 ms, floor(stop timeout / 2)) for force termination. Each process signal has its own bounded exit interval; completion acknowledgement has a separate drain grace.

5 s stop; 500 ms maximum reserve; 20 ms controller polling; 500 ms per SIGTERM/SIGKILL exit wait; 20 ms exit polling; 250 ms drain acknowledgement at 5 ms intervals.

Reason on record: The record states bounded stop escalation, preservation of small stop windows and an opportunity for attached clients to acknowledge.

Analyze 13 ↗
Which clock is running?
14
Pass idle lifetime as a policy projection
STATED
PLAYED

DaemonLifetime receives the shutdown section’s idleTimeoutMs.

BASE BEHAVIOR

Supply a free-standing number or use the CLI’s exported idle constant.

Thirty-minute idle lifetime keeps its existing navigation semantics: accepted navigation and the queue becoming idle control the timer; an active navigation is allowed to finish.

A Pick of one shutdown leaf is enough for this consumer. The class keeps its timer and callback; only threshold ownership changes.

Reason on record: The policy record releases retained resources after inactivity; the PR explicitly moves idle lifetime onto a required lifecycle slice.

Analyze 14 ↗
What is retained?
15
Bound diagnostics without expiring results
STATED
PLAYED

Logger and disconnected traces consume diagnostic limits; result retention remains separate.

COACH’S VARIATION · HYPOTHETICAL

Use trace expiry or log capacity to decide whether completed output survives.

Log rotation and queue size are policy inputs. Trace expiry discards diagnostic state, not the completion spool; trace capacity retains an effective minimum of one.

10 MiB active-log rotation; four backups; 1,024 queued events; five-minute disconnected traces; 1,024 traces with max(1, value). Logger queue overflow test is added.

Reason on record: The record bounds diagnostic memory/history and retains reconnect evidence without changing result retention; result eviction is deferred.

What can a test ask for?
16
Put the old convenience API behind tests
STATED
PLAYED

Seven helper files adapt legacy test knobs to validated policy snapshots.

ALTERNATIVE NAMED IN PR

Keep production compatibility overloads for those tests.

Production composition must provide policy. Existing unit, integration, e2e and benchmark callers can retain convenient test constructors. Logger and spool wrappers also live in test files.

Helpers cover controller, process terminator, registry, resource policy, startup coordinator, local transport and workspace daemon. Test factory validates by the existing serialized-policy codec.

Reason on record: The PR says tests need small thresholds without restoring runtime tuning seams.

UNEXPLAINED
PLAYED

Normalize zero/tiny inline values, adjust records, and pre-create the client directory.

COACH’S VARIATION · HYPOTHETICAL

Preserve the old forced-spill setup with explicit valid chunks and a witnessed file.

Transport helper maps inline 0 → 64 KiB and mkdirs the output directory. A one-chunk 64 KiB cleanup test now stays inline; an empty directory alone does not witness a removed spill file.

Capture comparison uses 32 B instead of 1 B; aggregate-spool test inline rises 1→6 B; zero-inline spool tests gain positive thresholds/extra writes; capacity fixture “xx” splits into “x”, “x”. Workspace helper rescales chunk/inline/result bounds.

Reason not found: Validation explains why the old zero-inline policy is invalid; no stated reason was found for these exact fixture substitutions or the directory creation.

PLAYED

COACH’S VARIATION · HYPOTHETICAL

Keep an explicit mapping from retired cases to the central policy oracle.

Five memory table rows, one constraint test and one 250 ms constant assertion disappear. Central policy tests already cover the formulas and defaults; the exact 256 MiB row is absent there.

Existing central table uses 1 byte, 512 MiB, 1 GiB, 16 GiB and 64 GiB. Consumer 250 ms timing test remains; a custom 17 ms / 103,102,101-byte threshold test is added.

PLAYED

Drop startupTimeoutMs from production and from healthy-wait fixtures.

Replace the fixture’s short knob with an explicit policy-based grace crossing.

The healthy-wait test still waits 25 ms and asserts it is unsettled, but no longer supplies 5 ms. Base only declared and assigned that knob; it never read it.

PLAYED

Translate that legacy cap into resources, or remove it from test call sites.
